speaker: Doctor
text: Given the deeper ache in the ear canal and the shooting pain triggered by eating, I suspect involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve or tensor tympani muscle irritation. Do you experience any clicking or popping sounds in your ear during these painful episodes, and has the pain worsened or improved since the surgery?

text: I don't hear any clicking or popping sounds, but the pain has definitely improved since the surgery. The audiology report from last week showed a 20-decibel improvement in my hearing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the pain has improved and hearing has recovered, the surgical outcome appears successful, but the residual sensitivity suggests localized nerve irritation or scar tissue formation. Is the pain strictly limited to the moments you are chewing, or does it persist for a short duration afterward?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain is strictly limited to the moments I am chewing and goes away immediately after. It doesn't linger or persist once I stop eating.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the strict correlation with chewing and the absence of other symptoms, this points toward auriculotemporal nerve irritation rather than a structural failure. Since the chief physician has confirmed Z-Syndrome and restricted further testing, I will proceed with the diagnosis based on the clinical picture.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia secondary to tympanoplasty
